sentences.zh: 首先，你看着，你把那个想法说出来，好吧，我老板再也不会信任我了。

sentences.en: First of all, you look, you say that thought, okay, my boss is never going to trust me again.
sentences.zh: 现在你的任务是，首先，找出支持那个想法的所有证据。

sentences.en: Now what your task is, is first of all, to identify all of the evidence that you have that supports that thought.
sentences.zh: 你现在在笑，对吧？

sentences.en: Now you're laughing, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你意识到这个想法有多荒谬，比方说荒谬，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you recognize that the more ridiculous the thought is, let's say ridiculous, right?
sentences.zh: 这个想法越缺乏证据支持，显然你能写出来支持这个想法的事情就会越少。

sentences.en: The less evidence-based the thought is, obviously the fewer things you're going to be able to put down to support that thought.
sentences.zh: 然后你要做的是，一旦你完成了那一列，现在你必须找出所有不支持该想法的证据。

sentences.en: Then what you do, so once you're done with that column, now what you have to do is identify all of the evidence that does not support the thought.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种事以前发生过。

sentences.en: You know, this has happened before.
sentences.zh: 我的老板一直很信任我。

sentences.en: My boss has continued to trust me.
sentences.zh: 我干得很出色。

sentences.en: I've done a great job.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我以前有过其他成功的项目。

sentences.en: You know, I've had other successful projects.
sentences.zh: 我的老板喜欢我。

sentences.en: My boss likes me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果他/她不喜欢我，他/她就不会在这么重要的项目上信任我，等等，等等，等等。

sentences.en: You know, if he or she didn't like me, he or she wouldn't trust me on such important projects, et cetera, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 所以不可避免地，结果就是你手里只有一张非常短的支持负面想法的证据清单。

sentences.en: So inevitably what happens is you have this very short list of evidence that supports the negative thought.
sentences.zh: 而你有一张非常长的不支持负面想法的证据清单。

sentences.en: And you have a very long list of evidence that does not support the negative thought.
sentences.zh: 接下来是最后一步，正如科学家会做的那样，那就是评估，审视

sentences.en: And then there's the final step, as a scientist would do, which is that to evaluate, to look
sentences.zh: 你产生那个负面想法，审视支持它的证据，审视

sentences.en: at that negative thought you had, to look at the evidence that supports it, to look at the
sentences.zh: 不支持它的证据，然后根据证据的权衡来重写那个想法。

sentences.en: evidence that does not support it, and then to rewrite that thought now based on the balance of the evidence.
sentences.zh: 所以如果最初的想法是，我老板再也不会信任我了，因为我搞砸了，

sentences.en: So if the original thought was, my boss is never going to trust me again because I messed up,
sentences.zh: 重写后的想法会更加平衡，更有证据支持，听起来会类似于，犯错是在所难免的。

sentences.en: the rewritten thought would be much more balanced and much more evidence-based and sound something like, mistakes sometimes happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在尽我最大的努力。

sentences.en: You know, I'm doing my beSt.
sentences.zh: 我是团队中受重视的一员，我的老板理解，你知道，我在尽力，而且，你知道，失败是成功的一部分，等等等等。

sentences.en: I'm a valued member of the team, and my boss understands that, you know, I'm doing my best and, you know, that, you know, failing is part of success and blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许我刚才说得不够生动，但我想要强调的是，那些“等等等等”的部分确实不够生动。

sentences.en: You know, maybe I didn't say that so eloquently, but I want to highlight the blah, blah, blah part wasn't very eloquent.
sentences.zh: 但我想强调的是，重写后的想法应该是你真正加工了情况的现实之后的结果。

sentences.en: But what I want to highlight is that that rewritten thought should be the result of you processing really what the reality of the situation is.
sentences.zh: 最后，你只需要努力去认同那些更有证据支持的想法。

sentences.en: And then finally, you just need to work on owning those thoughts that are much more evidence-based.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这就像骑自行车一样。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's like riding a bike.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你第一次进行这种认知重构时，它需要大量的时间和精力。

sentences.en: You know, when you first do this cognitive restructuring, it involves a lot of time and effort.
sentences.zh: 你需要把你的想法写下来，并把你自己和它们隔离开来。

sentences.en: You need to write your thoughts down and sort of separate yourself from them.
sentences.zh: 实际上，你知道，你真的可以把支持和反对该想法的证据写在纸上，这样你就能真正接受它。

sentences.en: And you actually, you know, you can actually write the evidence that's for and the evidence that's against the thought on paper so that you can own it.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你熟练掌握了它，就像骑自行车一样，你就会学会自动地做到这一点，

sentences.en: But once you get good at it, just like riding a bike, you sort of learn to do this automatically
sentences.zh: 也就是当你走在路上时，那个想法会突然蹦出来，而你则会抓住自己。

sentences.en: where you'll just be walking along and that thought will pop up and you'll catch yourself.
sentences.zh: 你会说，哇，哇，哇，这想得也太远了。

sentences.en: And you'll say, whoa, whoa, whoa, that's really out there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我知道我此刻确实有这种感觉，但让我们退一步，检查一下这个想法是否真的，你知道，这个想法在多大程度上是真的。

sentences.en: You know, I know I'm feeling that in the moment, but let's take a step back and examine whether that thought is actually, you know, to what extent that thought is actually true.
sentences.zh: 因此，你将获得一种能力，基本上能够在街上行走的同时，当场进行这种认知重构。

sentences.en: And so you'll gain the ability to basically do that cognitive restructuring in the moment while you're walking down the street.
sentences.zh: 然后，那个想法不再困扰你五分钟、十分钟、一天、两天，而是突然之间，你达到了这样一种境界，即所谓地非常迅速地重写了那个想法，

sentences.en: And then instead of that thought bothering you for five, 10 minutes, one day, two days, all of a sudden you get to the point where you quote unquote rewrite that thought so quickly
sentences.zh: 以至于你处于那种负面情绪状态的时间只有两分钟，而不是两小时或两天。

sentences.en: that you only are in that negative emotional state for two minutes rather than two hours or two days.
sentences.zh: 你真正重新训练了自己如何去面对并克服它。

sentences.en: You really retrained yourself how to face it and get past it.
sentences.zh: 这是很好的建议。

sentences.en: That's good advice.
sentences.zh: 那么让我转向你做过大量工作的另一个研究领域，也就是关于压力的测量。

sentences.en: So let me move to another area of research where you've done a lot of work, which is around the measurement of stress.
sentences.zh: 你开发了一种叫做“压力与逆境量表”的工具，旨在量化人们一生中接触到的压力。

sentences.en: You've developed something called the Stress and Adversity Inventory, which aims to quantify people's lifetime exposure to stress.
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈为什么能够量化和测量压力如此重要，以及这个量表是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: Can you talk about why it's important to be able to quantify and measure stress and how the inventory works?
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 所以在医学的其他任何领域，你绝对不会，例如在外科手术中，你绝对不会把人切开，或者你绝不会说服别人接受手术，

sentences.en: So in any other area of medicine, you would never, for example, in surgery, you would never cut somebody open or you may never convince somebody to be cut open
sentences.zh: 如果你没有给他们任何理由来解释为什么这个手术是必要的。

sentences.en: if you didn't give them some reason for why the surgery was necessary.
sentences.zh: 你还必须做出决定，即你应该多么重视这种治疗，或者某种特定治疗在你的优先事项列表中应该排在多高的位置。

sentences.en: You also have to make decisions about how much you should really care about the treatment or how high on the priority list a particular treatment should be.
sentences.zh: 或者对于侵入性干预措施而言，

sentences.en: Or for interventions that are invasive,
sentences.zh: 现在及早干预与等待一段时间相比，成本效益是怎样的。

sentences.en: what the cost benefit is to intervening quickly and now versus waiting a while.
sentences.zh: 我用这个类比是因为我认为在医学的其他领域，你绝不可能让人们参与某种特定的治疗，

sentences.en: I use this analogy because I think that in other areas of medicine, you would never get people to engage in a particular treatment
sentences.zh: 甚至让他们理解这种治疗有多重要，除非你给他们一个硬性指标，说明他们的状况有多好或多糟。

sentences.en: or even to understand how important the treatment is if you didn't give them a hard metric about how well or how poorly they were doing.
sentences.zh: 所以在癌症肿瘤的例子中，如果你，你知道，对那个肿瘤进行成像，然后和患者坐在一起，

sentences.en: So in the case of a cancerous tumor, for example, if you, you know, image that tumor and you sit down with a patient
sentences.zh: 把那个肿瘤的X光片或其他成像放到板上，然后你说，你知道，过去六个月你感觉真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: and you put an x-ray or some other imaging of that tumor up on the board and you say, you know, you've been feeling really crappy for the past six months.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，原因在于你体内有一个癌性肿瘤。

sentences.en: The reason for that, unfortunately, is that you have this cancerous tumor inside of you.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想告诉你的是，我们有一种治疗技术能够解决这个问题，但这需要你付出很大的动力。

sentences.en: Now, I want to let you know that we have this therapeutic technique that is going to be able to take care of that, but it's going to require a lot of motivation on your part.
sentences.zh: 它需要坚持一种不那么轻松的治疗方案，

sentences.en: It's going to require adhering to a treatment that is not going to be, you know, that is going to require a lot of effort, but it has a high success rate.
sentences.zh: 这需要付出很大的努力，但它有很高的成功率。

sentences.en: So if you stick with me and stick with this treatment for six months, we're going to get through this together and you're going to feel much better.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你听我的，坚持这个疗程六个月，我们将一起度过难关，你会感觉好多了。

sentences.en: Now, all of a sudden, when you have that metric, you fully understand what the hell is going on and why you should garner up the motivation to get on the treatment plan
sentences.zh: 现在，突然之间，当你有了这个指标，你就完全明白了到底是怎么回事，以及为什么要积聚动力来加入治疗计划，

sentences.en: and to really see this through.
sentences.zh: 并真正坚持到底。

sentences.en: And actually, you know, reducing your stress and moving toward wellness in life, you know, not trying to make the analogy that being really stressed out is better
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，减轻你的压力并走向人生的健康，你知道，我并不是在做类比，说压力大比

sentences.en: or worse than having cancer, but you can also die from stress.
sentences.zh: 患癌症更好或更糟，但压力也是会死人的。

sentences.en: And for some of us, stress can really be quite impactful and stress can also come from a lot of sources, being in a terrible relationship,
sentences.zh: 对我们中的一些人来说，压力确实会产生很大的影响，而且压力也可能来自很多来源，比如身处一段糟糕的感情中、

sentences.en: having the nasty boss, having a job that is not bringing us joy,
sentences.zh: 有一个刻薄的老板、有一份带给我们不到快乐的工作、

sentences.en: taking on too many responsibilities at work,
sentences.zh: 在工作中承担了太多的责任、

sentences.en: having difficult financial situations.
sentences.zh: 面临困难的财务状况。

sentences.en: And what I want to say is that in order to be motivated to really realign our life with our purpose,
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，为了有动力真正让我们的生活与我们的目标重新对齐，

sentences.en: if you like the idea of dharma, to identify whether or not we're really pursuing our dharma, whether or not we are living the life to the fullest in the way that we really,
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢“法”（dharma）的概念，即识别我们是否真的在追求我们的“法”，我们是否在以真正有意义、

sentences.en: that is meaningful and that brings us joy and purpose,
sentences.zh: 能带给我们快乐和目标的方式充实地生活，

sentences.en: requires a lot of motivation and time and effort.
sentences.zh: 这需要大量的动力、时间和精力。

sentences.en: And so long, it's my monologue again, I apologize.
sentences.zh: 好了，我又开始长篇大论了，非常抱歉。

sentences.en: But what I want to say is that the reason you need to assess stress clearly and with a clear metric is that, first of all, you need to build motivation
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是，你需要清晰地评估压力并提供明确指标的原因是，首先，你需要建立动力

sentences.en: for making difficult changes in life.
sentences.zh: 来对生活做出艰难的改变。

sentences.en: That's the point.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: And if you don't assess it, then you can't address it.
sentences.zh: 如果你不评估它，你就无法解决它。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to get somebody on board with making difficult changes in their life or adhering to a challenging treatment regimen
sentences.zh: 要让某人接受在生活中做出艰难的改变，或者坚持具有挑战性的治疗方案，是非常困难的，

sentences.en: if you don't know what the magnitude of the problem is.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道问题的严重程度的话。

sentences.en: And so, for example, if I say that I'm stressed out,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果我说我压力很大，

sentences.en: I'm really stressed out.
sentences.zh: 我压力真的很大。

sentences.en: Well, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是什么意思？

sentences.en: I'm on a scale from one to 10.
sentences.zh: 在一到十的量表上，

sentences.en: Does that mean I'm a three out of 10?
sentences.zh: 这意味我是十分之三吗？

sentences.en: Or does that mean I'm a nine out of 10?
sentences.zh: 还是意味着我是十分之九？

sentences.en: And if a nine out of 10 means that my risk for having a cardiac event, a heart attack, you know, in the next five years is now 85%,
sentences.zh: 如果十分之九意味着我在未来五年内发生心脏事件、心脏病的风险现在是85%，

sentences.en: well, all of a sudden, that's going to motivate me quite strongly
sentences.zh: 那么，突然之间，这将极大地激励我

sentences.en: to look at my stress levels in an objective way as compared to somebody else, understand, you know, whether or not my stress is higher than normal,
sentences.zh: 以客观的方式审视我的压力水平，与其他人进行比较，了解我的压力是高于正常水平还是低于正常水平，

sentences.en: less, you know, lower than normal, and also, you know, in which areas of my life I can make positive changes.
sentences.zh: 并且也知道我可以在生活的哪些方面做出积极的改变。

sentences.en: And that's really what the stress and adversity inventory is all about, the strain, which is about
sentences.zh: 这正是压力与逆境量表（strain）的全部意义所在，它致力于

sentences.en: creating concrete metrics,
sentences.zh: 创建具体的指标。

sentences.en: population level metrics, to understand how much stress have you actually experienced as compared to other people of similar gender and age, et cetera,
sentences.zh: 人口水平的指标，用于了解与同性别、同年龄等其他人相比，你实际经历过多大的压力，

sentences.en: so that when you're feeling really stressed out, you can estimate in a concrete way your actual health risks that are associated with stress.
sentences.zh: 这样当您感到压力山大时，您就能以具体的方式评估与压力相关的实际健康风险。

sentences.en: And so the inventory involves looking at the stressors that you have experienced across your whole lifespan.
sentences.zh: 因此，这项评估包括回顾你一生中所经历的压力源。

sentences.en: I mean, is that what you're trying to do and then give people a number to say that, you know, you're an eight and you're going to have a heart attack in five years, like you said,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这正是你想要做的吗，然后给人们一个数字，比如，你知道的，你是八级，五年后你就会心脏病发作，就像你说的，

sentences.en: unless you'd make a change in your life?
sentences.zh: 除非你在生活中做出改变？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: The lifetime part is really important because if you go online and you take these stress measures,
sentences.zh: “一生”这一部分非常重要，因为如果你上网去做这些压力测试，

sentences.en: and, you know, by the way, there are a bazillion of them online,
sentences.zh: 而且，顺便说一句，网上的这类测试多得数不清，

sentences.en: the amount of time period that's covered by those questions is really important.
sentences.zh: 这些问题所涵盖的时间跨度非常重要。

sentences.en: So, for example, some of them only focus on things that happened to you before age 18.
sentences.zh: 例如，其中一些只关注你在18岁之前发生的事情。

sentences.en: And we know that early life stress is really important.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，早年生活受到的压力确实非常重要。

sentences.en: It's when the brain and the body are developing.
sentences.zh: 那是大脑和身体发育的时期。

sentences.en: And so if you've experienced a lot of early life stress, your brain and body, you know, develop to be, for example, more threat sensitive maybe than somebody who hasn't
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你经历过很多早年压力，你的大脑和身体，就会发育得，比如，可能比那些没有经历过

sentences.en: experienced those stressors.
sentences.zh: 这些压力源的人对威胁更加敏感。

sentences.en: But, you know,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，

sentences.en: I'm here to tell you that stress doesn't end when you turn 18.
sentences.zh: 我是来告诉你，压力不会在你满18岁时结束。

sentences.en: So if you're only assessing stress early in life, you may be missing out on 10, 20, 30, 50 years of stress exposure.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你只评估早期的压力，你可能会漏掉10年、20年、30年甚至50年的压力暴露。

sentences.en: Other instruments online ask you about things that you might have experienced over the past week.
sentences.zh: 网上的其他工具会询问你过去一周可能经历过的事情。

sentences.en: And those things that experienced over the past week may be really relevant for how anxious or sad or disconnected you feel right now.
sentences.zh: 而过去一周经历的这些事情，可能与你现在感到焦虑、悲伤或脱节的程度息息相关。

sentences.en: But a lot of the biology that underpins chronic disease is much more prolonged and persistent and slowly developing.
sentences.zh: 但支撑慢性病的许多生物学机制要漫长得多、持续得多，而且是缓慢发展的。

sentences.en: So only assessing stressors that occur over the past week may not be sufficient for really coming to an estimate of chronic disease risk simply because it's the chronic stressors
sentences.zh: 因此，仅评估过去一周内发生的压力源可能不足以真正估算出慢性病风险，很简单，因为正是那些

sentences.en: that are around in our lives for much longer than a week that really engage the immune system, upregulate inflammation,
sentences.zh: 在我们生活中持续时间远超一周的慢性压力源，才会真正激活免疫系统、上调炎症反应，

sentences.en: cause oxidative stress, lead to the development of cancer tumors and biological aging and et cetera.
sentences.zh: 引发氧化应激，导致肿瘤生长和生物学老化等。

sentences.en: So you really need a panoramic snapshot, I think, of all of the things you've experienced over your entire life course.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，你确实需要对你一生中所经历的所有事情有一个全景式的快照。

sentences.en: And that's what an instrument like the Stress and Adversity
sentences.zh: 而这就是像《压力与逆境

sentences.en: Inventory affords us.
sentences.zh: 量表》这样的工具所能为我们提供的。

sentences.en: So I want to talk for a minute about some other research that you've done that still shows a connection between stress and health.
sentences.zh: 所以我想花几分钟时间聊聊你做过的一些其他研究，这些研究仍然表明压力与健康之间存在联系。

sentences.en: And that's a study that you did on how acetaminophen, which most of us know as Tylenol, might affect people who have experienced social rejection.
sentences.zh: 这是一项关于对乙酰氨基酚（我们大多数人知道的泰诺）如何影响经历过社会排斥的人的研究。

sentences.en: Can you talk about those findings?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这些发现吗？

sentences.en: Because I think they're fascinating.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得它们太迷人了。

sentences.en: Thanks for bringing that up.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你提起这个。

sentences.en: So we ran a clinical trial a few years ago where we essentially followed individuals over time and we randomly assigned the participants in this study to take acetaminophen
sentences.zh: 几年前我们做过一项临床试验，基本上是随访了一段时间的个体，我们随机分配研究中的参与者在其中一组中连续几周服用对乙酰氨基酚

sentences.en: for several weeks in one group or to not take, to basically take a placebo pill in the other group.
